GLAND & CYST CARE

Bartholin’s cyst treatment

Understand assessment, drainage and care for a recurring cyst.

AT A GLANCE

What this care addresses

A Bartholin’s cyst can appear as a lump on one side near the vaginal opening. Some are painless; an infection can cause an abscess. Have a new lump checked rather than assuming its cause.

Patient information · Canada · Sources checked 8 September 2026

What this care addresses

A Bartholin’s cyst can appear as a lump on one side near the vaginal opening. Some are painless; an infection can cause an abscess. Have a new lump checked rather than assuming its cause.

NHS · Bartholin’s cyst ↗

Assessment and care options

Some cysts need no treatment. Depending on infection and recurrence, care may include antibiotics or drainage. A clinician may place a small catheter or create an opening for continued drainage. Do not squeeze or drain a cyst yourself.

When to arrange care

Seek urgent care if a lump rapidly becomes larger or more painful, contains pus, or comes with fever or feeling unwell.

NHS · Bartholin’s cyst ↗

Questions for your appointment

  • What confirms the diagnosis?
  • Why do you recommend this drainage approach?
  • What is the plan if it returns?

Planning a conversation in Canada

Ask your clinician where an assessment can be arranged and whether a referral is required. Confirm service availability, fees and any coverage directly with the provider and your insurer or provincial plan.
